newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower, semiconductor shrs tumble.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower, semiconductor shrs tumble.

text.p: Stocks closed weaker on Saturday as a news report on semiconductor price falls sparked sales of chip shares, leading to an overall index slide, brokers said.
"News of semiconductor price falls hit chip makers' shares," said Na Min-ho, a broker at Daishin Securities.
Domestic Seoul Economic Daily reported that the unit price for the 16-megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) dropped to $6.9 from $7 level in May, quoting the American IC Exchange.
The composite index closed 9.82 points lower at 760.40.
Samsung Electronics, the world's leading memory maker, fell 1,600 won to 68,400.
LG Semicon dropped 1,100 won to 35,700, and Hyundai Electronics lost 1,400 won to 46,000.
"Consolidation is likely to continue for the time being," said Lee Young-won of Daewoo Securities.
Volume totalled 23.4 million shares for Saturday's half-day trading, compared with 42.2 million on Friday.
Trading was suspended for about an hour due to computer sytem problems.
Na of Daishin forecast the index would test 740 next week.
